gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Fanttik E1 Max costs $44.97 on fanttik.com today (2026-11-14). That makes the E1 Max cheaper than the HOTO ADV ($49.99, 25 bits) and the Ryobi Microtech ChatGPT offered as the 'alternative around $50' ($49.97), so ChatGPT's top pick now undercuts its own budget alternatives.
standout_why: Pages checked: the cited fanttik.com 'HOTO vs Fanttik' blog lists the E1 Max at $59.97 'at time of writing' with no date and gives no HOTO figures. toolengineers.com (rank 1 in every chat) shows '—' for every price. Every ChatGPT answer showed the E1 Max at $59.97 and the E2 Ultra at $79.99, and our own page (prices dated 2026-11-06) shows the same two stale prices. None of these has today's prices or the fact that the E1 Max now costs less than the HOTO ADV and the Ryobi. It is a Black Friday early-bird price, so it is useful but temporary. It confirms the pick rather than overturning it.
decides: It confirms the E1 Max as the pick for phones, cameras and small gadgets and removes the reason to recommend a ~$50 alternative. At $44.97 it costs $5.02 less than the HOTO ADV, which has the same 0.05/0.2 N·m torque but half the bits (25 vs 50) and is slower (170 vs 200 RPM). The step up to the E2 Ultra for laptops and PCs is now $25.02 ($69.99 vs $44.97), not $20.02. The iFixit driver at $22.95 stays the under-$30 pick only for people who already own 4 mm bits.
